name: aomega-m3-gate3-determinant-ladder
description: The pretzel's pairing determinant ladder derived from the Casoratian ratio, the SL-vs-GL rule it implies calibrated against GGM's two printed choices, and the GL-not-SL prediction at rank 6.

parameters.identity: det G_{M,L} = ratio^M ratio_bar^L det J c

verdict: GATE 3, partially closed and honestly bounded. det G_{M,L} = ratio^M ratio_bar^L det J c, so the entire index dependence is the Casoratian ratio and nothing else. That yields a rule — trivial dependence <=> SL possible, nontrivial => GL and never SL — which reproduces GGM's OWN two printed choices, GL for 4_1 in (138) and SL for 5_2 at u=0 in (93) (G1, two-for-two, calibrated before use). Applied to the pretzel with Part 1's ratio q^4: det G_{M,L} = q^{4(M-L)} det J c, a nonconstant unit monomial, so the rank-6 pairing is GL and CANNOT be SL off the diagonal (G2) — a derived prediction, since no held source prints a rank-6 pairing. Note the pretzel groups with 4_1 here (index-DEPENDENT determinant) exactly as it does on Part 9's branch structure: two independent groupings agreeing. What does NOT close (T1): det J and c individually, which need the explicit rank-6 blocks.

assertions.name: G1-the derived rule (index dependence trivial <=> SL possible) reproduces GGM's OWN two printed choices — GL(2, Z[q,x]) for 4_1 in (138) and SL(3, Z[q]) for 5_2 at u=0 in (93) — so it is calibrated on published statements before being applied at rank 6

G2-the pretzel's determinant ladder is q^{4(M-L)} times a constant: a NONCONSTANT unit monomial, so GL membership holds automatically on determinant grounds and SL is IMPOSSIBLE off the diagonal M = L

T1-gate 3 closes COMPLETELY, i.e. det J and c are individually determined. It does NOT: the ladder constrains how they enter, not either factor. Closing them needs the explicit rank-6 blocks or a printed rank-6 pairing, and no held source prints one
assertions.what_is_closed: the determinant ladder q^{4(M-L)} and the GL-not-SL verdict
assertions.what_is_open: det J and c = det W_0(q) det W_0(q^-1) individually
assertions.searched: GGM secs 007/011/015/017 — pairings printed only at rank 2 (137)/(138) and rank 3 (92)/(93); Theorem 28 gives the general operator and W but no pairing
